title: Pinned real Ribasim priority allocation followed by physical realization shortfall

sequencing.meaning: DUMMY-19D is closed. DUMMY-19E executable implementation is bound to this post-DUMMY-19D repository head; scientific expectations remain those frozen before DUMMY-19D completed.

purpose: Combine the qualified DUMMY-19B management scarcity mechanism with the qualified DUMMY-19C common-factor physical reduction mechanism. Test whether Ribasim first fixes priority-based allocation and then physically reduces only those allocated paths, without automatically reallocating allocated-but-unsupplied water within the same one-day allocation window.

independent_continuous_reference.ode: A dh/dtau = 32 * (1 - phi(h-0.99)), tau in days, because total allocated target is 32 m3/day in both priority cases and all active allocated links share one physical reduction factor.
independent_continuous_reference.ledger: 32 m3 fixed inflow = total physical UserDemand supply + Basin storage gain.

hypotheses: Management scarcity is resolved first: root-first allocates 32/0 m3/day and external-first allocates 12/20 m3/day, reproducing DUMMY-19B.
The common physical min_level factor then acts only on the already allocated Basin-to-UserDemand targets.
Total physical supply and Basin trajectory are identical in both priority cases because total allocation is 32 m3/day and all active recipient links share the same physical reduction factor.
Recipient physical supply follows the allocated split within each case: 100/0 percent in root-first and 37.5/62.5 percent in external-first.
Allocated-but-unsupplied water remains in the source Basin and is not automatically reallocated to an unsatisfied lower-priority claim during the same one-day allocation window.
Priority therefore controls the management allocation map, while source-state physics controls how much of each allocated transfer is actually realized.
measurements: direct Basin-to-root and Basin-to-external physical interval-mean linkflows
integrated recipient and total physical supplied volumes
Basin interval trajectory and final basin_state_data endpoint
forbidden: no change of the pinned Ribasim source
no changing supply, demands, min_level values, allocation interval, reference values or tolerances after observing DUMMY-19E output
no interpreting allocated-but-unsupplied volume as a physical transfer
no claim about reallocation across a shorter allocation interval

semantics: physical UserDemand total demand is bounded by already allocated demand
each inflow link uses user_demand.inflow_link_allocated as q_k_target when allocation is enabled
physical q_k is q_k_target multiplied by source low-storage factor and source_level-minus-min_level reduction_factor
the physical UserDemand formulation contains no recipient reallocation step after those multiplicative reductions
pinned_source_binding.research_consequence: Within one frozen allocation window, allocated-but-unrealized transfer is expected to remain physical source storage rather than be silently redirected to another UserDemand link.
